qs: what is allgit
Describe the allgit project.
allgit overview
can you explain the overview of allgit
a: allgit is a next-generation version control system written in Rust: one global object graph, independent zones, and S3-backed remotes. The command is vcs and it has no git underneath.

qs: what language is allgit written in
In which programming language is allgit implemented?
allgit language
can you explain the language of allgit
a: allgit is written from scratch in Rust, requiring Rust 1.88 or newer. It has no git, libgit2 or Perforce underneath.

qs: what command does allgit use
What is the name of the allgit command line tool?
allgit command name
can you explain the command name of allgit
a: allgit's command is vcs (the README title is vcs), and the repository is Bobliuuu/allgit. A second binary, git-remote-allgit, ships in the vcs-cli crate.

qs: where is the allgit repo
Provide the GitHub URL for allgit.
allgit github link
can you explain the github link of allgit
a: allgit lives at https://github.com/Bobliuuu/allgit.

qs: who made allgit
Who is the author of allgit?
allgit author
can you explain the author of allgit
a: allgit is a repository by Jerry Zhu (GitHub: Bobliuuu), at github.com/Bobliuuu/allgit.

qs: why was allgit built
What problem does allgit aim to solve?
allgit purpose
can you explain the purpose of allgit
a: allgit is built for big repositories where code, art and docs should not share one history, where nobody wants to download everything, and where many people and agents push at once to an S3 bucket.

qs: what are zones in allgit
Explain the concept of zones in allgit.
allgit zones
can you explain the zones of allgit
a: In allgit a zone owns a path prefix such as engine/ or assets/ and has its own branches and history. Zones cannot overlap, so a busy art zone does not clutter the code log.

qs: how does allgit store objects
Describe the object model of allgit.
allgit global object graph
can you explain the global object graph of allgit
a: allgit uses one global content-addressed DAG. Every object (file chunk, tree, commit, transaction, operation) is named by its BLAKE3 hash and stored once, whichever zone or branch uses it.

qs: how does sparse subscription work in allgit
How can users download only part of an allgit repository?
allgit sparse subscription
can you explain the sparse subscription of allgit
a: In allgit you subscribe to the zones you need; skipped zones are never downloaded (and not deleted). Inside a zone, vcs sparse limits which paths are materialized.

qs: does allgit support atomic cross-zone commits
Explain atomic publishing in allgit.
allgit atomic publish
can you explain the atomic publish of allgit
a: allgit lets one commit change several zones, and vcs publish moves all the branch heads you publish in one step, or none. Objects upload first, then one compare-and-swap of the manifest.

qs: how does allgit use S3
What is the role of S3 in allgit's remote protocol?
allgit S3 remote
can you explain the S3 remote of allgit
a: allgit's remote can be a directory, an S3-compatible bucket or a vcs-server. A single manifest object replaced by compare-and-swap is the source of truth, and the bucket needs conditional writes (probed at connect).

qs: what is the allgit manifest
How does the compare-and-swap manifest work in allgit?
allgit CAS manifest
can you explain the CAS manifest of allgit
a: allgit's remote has one manifest object, replaced by conditional write, as the authority; a publish becomes visible at one instant. The protocol is checked by an executable model that explores crashes and interleavings.

qs: what is group commit in allgit
Describe the group commit feature of allgit.
allgit group commit
can you explain the group commit of allgit
a: In allgit, vcs-server merges disjoint publishes that arrive together into one manifest write; clients keep the txid protocol so a lost ack is safe. At 512 writers it gave 69.7 vs 27.3 publishes/s.

qs: does allgit have undo
How does allgit's operation log work?
allgit operation log
can you explain the operation log of allgit
a: allgit's vcs op log records every local change to branches and workspace, and vcs op undo and vcs op restore go back.

qs: how does allgit handle merge conflicts
Describe first-class conflicts in allgit.
allgit conflicts
can you explain the conflicts of allgit
a: In allgit a conflicted merge or rebase keeps conflicts as recorded state you can list, show and resolve (vcs conflict, vcs resolve), instead of leaving markers as the only record.

qs: does allgit support file locks
How do locks work in allgit?
allgit locks
can you explain the locks of allgit
a: allgit has vcs lock, unlock and locks for files that cannot be merged. Lock leases are enforced only when you publish through vcs-server; with a plain directory or bucket they are advisory.

qs: how does allgit handle large files
Describe the large-file engine in allgit.
allgit large files
can you explain the large files of allgit
a: allgit has a built-in large-file engine: big files are content-defined chunked, stored once, and added and checked out by streaming, with no separate large-file tool. Chunked objects are kind 9 with no format bump.

qs: how does garbage collection work in allgit
What does vcs gc do in allgit?
allgit garbage collection
can you explain the garbage collection of allgit
a: allgit's vcs gc deletes unreachable objects older than a grace period, locally and on remotes. vcs gc --dry-run reports what it would delete.

qs: does allgit work offline
Is allgit local-first?
allgit local-first
can you explain the local-first of allgit
a: allgit is local-first: everything except sharing works offline. Sharing is done with publish, fetch, sync and clone.

qs: what is novel about allgit
What does allgit claim to be genuinely new?
allgit what is new
can you explain the what is new of allgit
a: allgit believes the combination on one object model is new, plus zones as independent histories in one global graph, a zone ontology with automatic zone selection for agents, and an S3 bucket as sole authority via a CAS manifest with group commit.

qs: what is the allgit zone ontology
How do agents use zone ontology in allgit?
allgit zone ontology
can you explain the zone ontology of allgit
a: allgit's vcs zone describe/graph/explain/changes --json computes purpose, owners, dependencies, impact and recent changes from state vcs already has; nothing is stored or invented.

qs: what does clone --auto do in allgit
Explain automatic zone selection in allgit.
allgit auto zone selection
can you explain the auto zone selection of allgit
a: allgit's clone/sync --auto picks zones from a local, privacy-limited usage profile (zone id and directory prefix only; no model, no upload). Skipped zones stay listed.

qs: how much does allgit auto zone selection save
What download savings does allgit's zone profile achieve?
allgit auto zone numbers
can you explain the auto zone numbers of allgit
a: In allgit, cloning a 50-zone repo by usage profile moved 37.0 MB instead of 189.5 MB for a full clone. --auto downloads 19.5 percent of the bytes of a full vcs clone.

qs: how fast is allgit on 1 million files
Report allgit's benchmark results on a 1,000,000 file tree.
allgit 1M file benchmark
can you explain the 1M file benchmark of allgit
a: On a c6i.4xlarge, allgit cloned 1M files in 40.5 s vs git 603.1 s (not like for like), add 18.9 s vs 215.5 s, diff of a 1 percent change 3.7 s vs 19.7 s. A no-op add lost: 6.8 s vs 0.9 s.

qs: how fast is allgit add on 100k files
What is allgit's add time for 100,000 files?
allgit 100k add benchmark
can you explain the 100k add benchmark of allgit
a: allgit's add of 100,000 flat files took 733 ms vs git 5,383 ms (3 runs, fresh index).

qs: does allgit beat git in benchmarks
What is allgit's win/tie/loss scoreboard?
allgit scoreboard
can you explain the scoreboard of allgit
a: allgit totals 136 wins, 68 ties and 14 losses against git, Perforce, walgit, Jujutsu and Sapling. It says it is not uniformly faster than git.

qs: where does allgit lose
In which areas is allgit slower than git?
allgit losses
can you explain the losses of allgit
a: allgit's losses vs git include tiny metadata commands (branch, tag), ls-tree, bundle create, log --stat, gc CPU, add -u after a one-file change, no-op add at 1M files, and push throughput on local disk.

qs: how does allgit handle many pushers
What are allgit's results with 128 or more concurrent pushers?
allgit many writers
can you explain the many writers of allgit
a: allgit with 128 pushers to S3-compatible storage hit 42.2 pushes/s vs walgit 15.5, but on local disk 85.3 vs git 222.0 (a loss). On real S3 batch commit gave 157 to 348 pushes/s at 256 to 1024 writers.

qs: does allgit lose data on crashes
Is allgit durable under server kills?
allgit durability
can you explain the durability of allgit
a: allgit lost 0 acknowledged files when the server was kill -9'd 157 times in 14 minutes. A 64.7 GB monorepo stress test with 8 kills per run also lost none.

qs: how do I install allgit
What are the build and install steps for allgit?
allgit install
can you explain the install of allgit
a: Clone the repo, run cargo build --release (binaries in target/release) or cargo install --path crates/vcs-cli --locked to put vcs on PATH, then vcs --help. Needs Rust 1.88+.

qs: how do I get started with allgit
Give the allgit quickstart workflow.
allgit quickstart
can you explain the quickstart of allgit
a: allgit quickstart: set VCS_AUTHOR_NAME and VCS_AUTHOR_EMAIL, vcs init demo, create zones with vcs zone create, vcs add . and vcs commit, then vcs remote set, vcs publish, and vcs clone --zone engine.

qs: what crates make up allgit
What is the allgit repository layout?
allgit crates
can you explain the crates of allgit
a: allgit is a cargo workspace with vcs-objects, vcs-store, vcs-repo, vcs-remote, vcs-store-s3, vcs-merge, vcs-server, vcs-bench, vcs-cli and vcs-watchd, plus assist helper crates for Claude and OpenAI.

qs: what is vcs-server in allgit
What does the vcs-server binary do in allgit?
allgit server
can you explain the server of allgit
a: allgit's vcs-server is an HTTP validating writer that enforces locks and does group commit. It uses a thread per connection (256 default cap), and vcs-server --upstream makes a disk-cached peer tier.

qs: what is peering in allgit
How does allgit's read-through peering work?
allgit peering
can you explain the peering of allgit
a: allgit's vcs-server --upstream makes a disk-cached tier that forwards writes and serves immutable bytes locally. 64 to 256 concurrent clones cost the origin 3 requests with a warm peer vs 129 to 513 direct.

qs: does allgit use AI for merges
What is merge --assist in allgit?
allgit merge assist
can you explain the merge assist of allgit
a: allgit has opt-in helper binaries (vcs-assist-claude, vcs-assist-openai) for merge --assist. The Claude helper has never been called against the live API; the OpenAI one had one small live run.

qs: is allgit production ready
What is the maturity status of allgit?
allgit status
can you explain the status of allgit
a: allgit is early research software with no stable release and no on-disk format promise; object ids changed between early versions with no migration tool.

qs: what are allgit's limitations
List known limitations of allgit.
allgit limitations
can you explain the limitations of allgit
a: allgit's Windows support is only compile-checked in CI, and S3 was tested on MinIO, RustFS and AWS S3 only. Refs are fine to about 100k; 1M tags cost seconds per command.

qs: what license does allgit use
Under which license is allgit released?
allgit license
can you explain the license of allgit
a: allgit is licensed under either the Apache License 2.0 or the MIT license, at your option.

qs: how is allgit different from git
Compare allgit with git.
allgit git comparison
can you explain the git comparison of allgit
a: allgit has no git underneath: its own BLAKE3 object format, packs, index and wire protocol. Unlike git it has zones with independent histories, atomic multi-zone publish, an op log and first-class conflicts.

qs: how is allgit tested
What testing does allgit use?
allgit testing
can you explain the testing of allgit
a: allgit runs cargo fmt, cargo clippy with -D warnings and cargo test --workspace, which includes the protocol model checker. S3 tests use MinIO.

qs: what is bobliu-os
Describe the bobliu-os project.
bobliu-os overview
can you explain the overview of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os is a from-scratch 32-bit x86 OS: preemptive multitasking, COW fork, VFS, own filesystem, libc, shell, Lua, and DOOM. It is a hobby kernel written to learn how every layer fits.

qs: what language is bobliu-os written in
What programming languages does bobliu-os use?
bobliu-os language
can you explain the language of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os is written in C plus assembly, with no Linux and no glibc. The repo's main language is C.

qs: what cpu does bobliu-os target
Which architecture does bobliu-os run on?
bobliu-os architecture target
can you explain the architecture target of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os targets 32-bit x86 (i686), booting via GRUB Multiboot, and is run under QEMU.

qs: where is the bobliu-os repo
Give the GitHub link for bobliu-os.
bobliu-os github link
can you explain the github link of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os is at https://github.com/Bobliuuu/bobliu-os.

qs: who made bobliu-os
Who built bobliu-os?
bobliu-os author
can you explain the author of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os was built by Jerry Zhu (GitHub: Bobliuuu).

qs: why was bobliu-os built
What motivated bobliu-os?
bobliu-os purpose
can you explain the purpose of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os is a hobby kernel written to learn how every layer fits together, following the OSDev Creating an Operating System roadmap and then pushed well past it.

qs: can bobliu-os run doom
How does DOOM run on bobliu-os?
bobliu-os doom
can you explain the doom of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os runs Doom via doomgeneric plus Freedoom as a ring 3 process, with the framebuffer for output and raw scancodes in, at about 60 fps under QEMU. Run it with doom -warp 1 1 -skill 2.

qs: does bobliu-os have lua
What Lua support does bobliu-os have?
bobliu-os lua
can you explain the lua of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os includes a Lua 5.1 interpreter, e.g. lua -e with a for loop printing squares and square roots.

qs: can bobliu-os run neovim
Does bobliu-os port neovim?
bobliu-os neovim
can you explain the neovim of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os runs the real neovim 0.10.4, cross-built from source with libuv, luv, msgpack, tree-sitter and libvterm. It is slow to start under QEMU (about a minute and a half) and has an 8-colour terminal.

qs: how does bobliu-os boot
Describe the bobliu-os boot process.
bobliu-os boot
can you explain the boot of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os boots from GRUB via Multiboot 1 into kernel_main, which sets up GDT, IDT, PIC, PIT, PMM, paging, heap and TSS, mounts initrd, ramfs and bobfs, and spawns /bin/sh as pid 1.

qs: what scheduler does bobliu-os use
How does multitasking work in bobliu-os?
bobliu-os scheduler
can you explain the scheduler of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os has a preemptive round-robin scheduler with 50 ms slices driven by a 100 Hz PIT, using swtch() for context switching.

qs: does bobliu-os have copy-on-write fork
How is fork implemented in bobliu-os?
bobliu-os fork
can you explain the fork of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os implements copy-on-write fork with per-frame refcounts. The forktest program checks COW fork, exec, exit status and 40 forks without leaking frames.

qs: how does bobliu-os manage memory
Describe bobliu-os memory management.
bobliu-os memory
can you explain the memory of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os uses a bitmap physical memory manager, paging with the kernel identity-mapped for 256 MiB and per-process user space, and a first-fit heap with coalescing.

qs: what protections does bobliu-os have
What hardening features are in bobliu-os?
bobliu-os hardening
can you explain the hardening of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os has kernel-stack guard pages, CR0.WP, and ring 3 faults that kill only the offending process.

qs: what filesystem does bobliu-os have
Describe bobfs in bobliu-os.
bobliu-os filesystem
can you explain the filesystem of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os has bobfs, its own on-disk filesystem (1 KiB blocks, 128 inodes, 12 direct + 1 indirect) mounted on /disk, on top of an ATA PIO driver exposed as /dev/hd0.

qs: does bobliu-os have a vfs
How is storage organized in bobliu-os?
bobliu-os vfs
can you explain the vfs of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os has a VFS with a mount table over a read-only tar initrd on /, ramfs on /tmp, bobfs on /disk, devfs and pipes.

qs: what shell does bobliu-os have
Describe the bobliu-os shell.
bobliu-os shell
can you explain the shell of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os's sh is a userland ELF program with quoting, variable expansion, globbing, and/or/sequence/background operators, stderr redirection, if/for/while, scripts, and a raw-mode line editor with history and Tab completion.

qs: does bobliu-os have its own libc
What C library does bobliu-os use?
bobliu-os libc
can you explain the libc of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os has its own libc: stdio with floating-point printf, malloc, string, ctype, qsort, scanf family, setjmp, time, plus musl libm.

qs: how many programs does bobliu-os have
How many userland commands ship with bobliu-os?
bobliu-os programs
can you explain the programs of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os ships 88 programs, including ls cat grep sed sort uniq find diff xxd head tail tr cut xargs more expr test and printf.

qs: what editors run on bobliu-os
Which text editors are available on bobliu-os?
bobliu-os editors
can you explain the editors of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os has vi (normal, insert and : modes), kilo (antirez's editor with syntax highlighting, ported with 2 changed lines) and a ported neovim 0.10.4.

qs: does bobliu-os support threads
Does bobliu-os have pthreads and signals?
bobliu-os threads
can you explain the threads of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os has clone-style kernel threads, pthread create/join, mutex and condvar on a futex, plus signals (kill, signal, sigreturn, Ctrl-C).

qs: how do syscalls work in bobliu-os
Describe the bobliu-os syscall interface.
bobliu-os syscalls
can you explain the syscalls of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os syscalls are numbered like Linux i386 and invoked through int 0x80, covering process, file, fd, memory (brk), time and tty/display calls.

qs: does bobliu-os support pipes
How do pipes work in bobliu-os?
bobliu-os pipes
can you explain the pipes of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os pipes use a 4 KiB ring buffer, are blocking, support EOF/EPIPE, and fd inheritance works with dup and dup2.

qs: what display does bobliu-os use
What graphics does bobliu-os support?
bobliu-os display
can you explain the display of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os has an ANSI-capable VGA text terminal and a 640x480x32 linear framebuffer, with PS/2 keyboard input including raw key up/down events.

qs: how do I run bobliu-os
What are the steps to build and boot bobliu-os?
bobliu-os quickstart
can you explain the quickstart of bobliu-os
a: Install an i686-elf cross GCC, grub-mkrescue, xorriso, qemu-system-i386 and make; run ./iso.sh to build bobliu.iso, then ./qemu.sh to boot it in QEMU.

qs: what scripts does bobliu-os have
What do iso.sh and qemu.sh do in bobliu-os?
bobliu-os scripts
can you explain the scripts of bobliu-os
a: In bobliu-os, ./iso.sh builds libc, kernel, userland and initrd into bobliu.iso; ./qemu.sh runs iso.sh and boots QEMU; ./clean.sh removes build products.

qs: what boot options does bobliu-os offer
What entries are in the bobliu-os GRUB menu?
bobliu-os grub menu
can you explain the grub menu of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os GRUB entries: user shell (init=/bin/sh, default), kernel shell only, and noshell (no shell, keyboard ignored).

qs: how do I add a program to bobliu-os
How can a new userland program be added to bobliu-os?
bobliu-os adding programs
can you explain the adding programs of bobliu-os
a: Drop user/myprog.c into the bobliu-os repo, rerun ./iso.sh, then run myprog inside the OS.

qs: what tests does bobliu-os have
Which test programs exist in bobliu-os?
bobliu-os tests
can you explain the tests of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os includes in-OS tests such as forktest, fdtest, memtest, wtest, pipetest, sigtest, threadtest, timetest, polltest, stdiotest, floattest, ttytest, crash and posixtest (35 checks).

qs: what are bobliu-os limitations
List known limitations of bobliu-os.
bobliu-os limitations
can you explain the limitations of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os is single core with max 16 processes and 16 fds each; bobfs has 128 files and 268 KiB per file; no networking, sound or serial console; kernel-mode exceptions halt the machine.

qs: what is bobliu-os status
How complete is bobliu-os?
bobliu-os status
can you explain the status of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os is a hobby kernel. Roadmap phases I to III (including Doom, Lua, kilo and neovim) are done; phase IV (networking, sound, USB, GUI) is not started.

qs: is bobliu-os a linux replacement
What is the scope of bobliu-os?
bobliu-os scope
can you explain the scope of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os is a learning OS, not a Linux replacement: single core, VGA text plus linear framebuffer, PS/2 keyboard, at most 16 processes.

qs: what license is bobliu-os under
What is the bobliu-os license?
bobliu-os license
can you explain the license of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os's own code is MIT; vendored code (doomgeneric, Freedoom, Lua, kilo) keeps its own license.

qs: what does bobliu-os build on
What third-party projects does bobliu-os credit?
bobliu-os credits
can you explain the credits of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os credits the OSDev wiki, doomgeneric, Freedoom, kilo by antirez, Lua 5.1 and musl libm.

qs: how does bobliu-os handle interrupts
Describe interrupt handling in bobliu-os.
bobliu-os interrupts
can you explain the interrupts of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os has a GDT and TSS with ring 0/3 segments, an IDT with exceptions 0-31, a remapped 8259 PIC, a 100 Hz PIT and int 0x80 syscalls.

qs: what is the bobliu-os address space layout
How is bobliu-os virtual memory laid out?
bobliu-os memory layout
can you explain the memory layout of bobliu-os
a: In bobliu-os, the kernel plus a 256 MiB identity map is shared by every address space, user ELF segments and heap start at 0x10000000 and 0x20000000, and kernel stacks (16 KiB each) sit near 0xE0000000 behind guard pages.

qs: does bobliu-os track time
What time support does bobliu-os provide?
bobliu-os time
can you explain the time of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os has a CMOS RTC plus PIT clock, nanosleep and clock_gettime.

What directories does bobliu-os have?
bobliu-os repo layout
can you explain the repo layout of bobliu-os
a: bobliu-os directories: kernel/ (arch/i386 and kernel.c), libc/, third_party/ (kilo), user/ (sh, coreutils, vi, tests), doom/, lua/, toolchain/ and docs/.

nvim-in-nvim overview

nvim-in-nvim language

nvim-in-nvim author

nvim-in-nvim idea

nvim-in-nvim acceptance test

nvim-in-nvim processes
